question: What does Bajaj Finance commit to do when a customer remains dissatisfied after raising a complaint?

gold_references.title: Fair Practice Code (Version 7.1)
gold_references.section_title: 2. Key Commitments
gold_references.evidence_snippet: Telling customers' how to take their complaint forward if they are still not satisfied
gold_references.reference_notes: The code expressly commits to explaining the next complaint step when the customer is still dissatisfied.

expected_information: The company should tell customers how to take their complaint forward if they remain dissatisfied.

question: What should the lender's acknowledgement tell an applicant about the handling of a loan application?

gold_references.title: Fair Practice Code (Version 7.1)
gold_references.section_title: 4. Applications for loans and their processing
gold_references.evidence_snippet: The Company will have a system of giving acknowledgement for receipt of loan applications. The time frame within which loan applications will be disposed of will be indicated in the acknowledgement.
gold_references.reference_notes: Both receipt acknowledgement and the stated disposal timeframe are on PDF page 4.

expected_information: The applicant should receive acknowledgement of the application and an indicated timeframe for its disposal.

question: In what language must borrower communications be provided under this fair-practice code?

gold_references.title: Fair Practice Code (Version 7.1)
gold_references.section_title: 4. Applications for loans and their processing
gold_references.evidence_snippet: All communications to the borrower shall be in the vernacular language or a language as understood by the borrower.
gold_references.reference_notes: The page gives the borrower's language comprehension as the alternative to the vernacular.

expected_information: Communications should use the vernacular language or another language the borrower understands.

question: What key loan information must Bajaj Finance convey in writing when a loan is sanctioned?

gold_references.title: Fair Practice Code (Version 7.1)
gold_references.section_title: 5. Loan appraisal and terms/conditions
gold_references.evidence_snippet: The Company will convey in writing to the borrower in the vernacular language by means of sanction letter or otherwise, the amount of loan sanctioned along with the terms and conditions including annualised rate of interest and method of application thereof
gold_references.reference_notes: This supports the sanctioned amount, terms, annualised rate, and rate-application method.

expected_information: The borrower must receive the sanctioned amount and terms in writing, including the annualised interest rate and how it is applied.

question: Where must penal charges for late repayment or another borrower default be highlighted?

gold_references.title: Fair Practice Code (Version 7.1)
gold_references.section_title: 6. Penal Charges in Loan Accounts
gold_references.evidence_snippet: The Company will mention the penal charge which will be charged for late repayment and / or any other default on the part of the customer, in bold in the loan agreement.
gold_references.reference_notes: The code specifies the loan agreement and bold presentation.

expected_information: The applicable penal charge should be stated in bold in the loan agreement.

question: How must a lender handle changes to loan terms such as the disbursement schedule or interest rate?

gold_references.title: Fair Practice Code (Version 7.1)
gold_references.section_title: 7. Disbursement of loans including changes in terms and conditions
gold_references.evidence_snippet: The Company will give notice to the borrower in the vernacular language of any change in the terms and conditions including disbursement schedule, interest rates, service charges, prepayment charges etc. The Company will also ensure that changes in interest rates and charges are effected only prospectively.
gold_references.reference_notes: This provision requires borrower notice and prospective effect for rate/charge changes.

expected_information: The borrower should be notified in an understood language, and interest-rate or charge changes should apply prospectively.

question: When does the code require the lender to release a borrower's securities, and what qualification applies?

gold_references.title: Fair Practice Code (Version 7.1)
gold_references.section_title: 7. Disbursement of loans including changes in terms and conditions
gold_references.evidence_snippet: The Company will release all securities on repayment of all dues or on realisation of the outstanding amount of loan subject to any legitimate right or lien for any other claim
gold_references.reference_notes: Release follows repayment/realisation but is subject to a legitimate right or lien for another claim.

expected_information: Securities are released after all dues are repaid or the loan amount is realised, subject to a legitimate lien or other claim.

question: What cost information must Tata Capital Housing Finance disclose so a borrower can compare loan offers?

gold_references.title: Fair Practices Code (Version 3.0)
gold_references.section_title: 5. LOANS
gold_references.evidence_snippet: Thus, we shall disclose ‘all in cost’ inclusive of all charges involved in processing/ sanction of loan application in a transparent manner. It shall also be ensured that such charges/fees are non-discriminatory.
gold_references.reference_notes: The page lists interest and fee/charge disclosures and concludes that all-in processing/sanction costs must be transparent and non-discriminatory.

expected_information: Disclose all processing/sanction charges transparently and on a non-discriminatory basis so borrowers can compare offers.

question: If a change in loan terms disadvantages the customer, what option does Tata Capital Housing Finance provide?

gold_references.title: Fair Practices Code (Version 3.0)
gold_references.section_title: 5.4 Disbursement of loans including changes in terms and conditions
gold_references.evidence_snippet: If such change is to the disadvantage of the customer, he/she may within 60 days and without notice close his / her account or switch it without having to pay any extra charges or interest.
gold_references.reference_notes: The 60-day period and no-extra-charge condition are stated together in the source.

expected_information: Within 60 days, the customer may close or switch the account without notice or additional charges/interest.

question: Where must Shriram Finance explain how it grades borrower risk and why different rates are charged?

gold_references.title: Fair Practice Code 2023
gold_references.section_title: 1) Applications for loans and their processing
gold_references.evidence_snippet: The loan application form and the sanction letter issued to the customer shall disclose the approach for gradation of risks and rationale for charging different rates of interest to different categories of borrowers and the same shall also be made available on the web-site of the Company or published in the relevant newspapers.
gold_references.reference_notes: The code names the application form, sanction letter, website, or relevant newspapers as disclosure locations.

expected_information: Risk-grading approach and rationale for different borrower rates must be disclosed in the application and sanction letter and made available on the website or in relevant newspapers.

question: What governance duties does Shriram Finance's board have for grievance handling and Fair Practice Code compliance?

gold_references.title: Fair Practice Code 2023
gold_references.section_title: 6) Responsibility of Board of Directors
gold_references.evidence_snippet: Such a mechanism shall ensure that all disputes arising out of the decisions of Company’s functionaries are heard and disposed of at least at the next higher level. (b) The Board of Directors shall also provide for periodical review of the compliance of the FPC
gold_references.reference_notes: The provision assigns the board responsibility for the mechanism, next-level review of disputes, and periodic FPC/grievance reviews.

expected_information: The board must establish a grievance mechanism with disputes reviewed at least one level higher and provide periodic review of FPC compliance and grievance functioning.

question: What repossession safeguards must Shriram Finance include in a vehicle loan agreement?

gold_references.title: Fair Practice Code 2023
gold_references.section_title: 9) Repossession of vehicles financed by Company
gold_references.evidence_snippet: the terms and conditions of the contract/loan agreement shall also contain provisions regarding: i. Notice period before taking possession; ii. Circumstances under which the notice period can be waived; iii. The procedure for taking possession of the security; iv. A provision regarding final chance to be given to the borrower for repayment of loan before the sale / auction of the property
gold_references.reference_notes: The cited list includes notice/waiver conditions, possession procedure, and a final repayment opportunity before sale or auction.

expected_information: The contract should state notice and waiver conditions, the possession procedure, and a final chance to repay before sale/auction.

question: What must Tata Capital provide and explain to a prospective microfinance borrower before the loan contract is executed?

gold_references.title: Fair Practices Code for Microfinance Loans
gold_references.section_title: 1. Applications for Loans and their processing
gold_references.evidence_snippet: The Company shall provide a Key Facts Statement (KFS) to all prospective borrowers to help them take an informed view before executing the loan contract, as per the standardised format. The KFS shall be written in a language understood by such borrowers. Contents of KFS shall be explained to the borrower and an acknowledgement shall be obtained
gold_references.reference_notes: The KFS must use an understood language, be explained, and be acknowledged before contract execution.

expected_information: Provide the standardized KFS in a language the borrower understands, explain it, and obtain acknowledgement of understanding before contract execution.

question: Where should microfinance repayments normally be collected, and when may field staff collect at a borrower's home or workplace?

gold_references.title: Fair Practices Code for Microfinance Loans
gold_references.section_title: 2. Recovery
gold_references.evidence_snippet: Recovery shall be made at a designated/central place decided mutually by the borrower and the Company. However, field staff shall be allowed to make recovery at the place of residence or work of the borrower if the borrower fails to appear at the designated/ central designated place on two or more successive occasions.
gold_references.reference_notes: Home/work collection is a stated exception after at least two successive failures to appear at the mutually designated place.

expected_information: Use a mutually chosen designated/central place; home/work collection is permitted only after the borrower misses that place on two or more successive occasions.

question: What customer protections are objectives of Tata Capital's customer grievance policy?

gold_references.title: Merged Customer Service and Grievance Handling Policy
gold_references.section_title: 2. The objective of the policy is to ensure that
gold_references.evidence_snippet: All customers are always treated fairly and without bias; All issues raised by customers are dealt with courtesy and resolved on time; Customers are made completely aware of their rights so that they can opt for alternative remedies if they are not fully satisfied with our response or resolution to their complaint
gold_references.reference_notes: These three stated objectives cover fair treatment, timely courteous resolution, and awareness of alternative remedies.

expected_information: Fair and unbiased treatment, courteous timely handling, and awareness of alternative remedies when customers are dissatisfied.

question: In Tata Capital's grievance-handling SOP table, what is the maximum turnaround time for tagging a case as QRC after a customer requirement or concern is identified?

question: When can the finance company disclose a borrower's personal or transaction information without the borrower's authorization?

gold_references.title: Fair Practice Code 2023
gold_references.section_title: 4) Confidentiality
gold_references.evidence_snippet: The Company will not reveal transaction details to any other entity including other than the following exceptional cases: If the Company has to provide the information by legal, statutory or regulatory laws
gold_references.reference_notes: The provision protects information by default and lists legal, statutory, or regulatory requirements as an exception; other listed exceptions appear on the same page.

expected_information: Disclosure without authorization is limited to the policy's stated exceptions, including legal, statutory, or regulatory requirements and the other listed circumstances.

question: During microfinance debt collection, which calling hours are prohibited by the fair-practice code?

gold_references.title: Fair Practices Code for Microfinance Loans
gold_references.section_title: 2. Recovery
gold_references.evidence_snippet: Persistently calling the borrower and/ or calling the borrower before 9:00 a.m. and after 6:00 p.m.
gold_references.reference_notes: This is listed among harsh recovery methods the company or its agent must not use.

expected_information: Do not persistently call borrowers or call before 9:00 a.m. or after 6:00 p.m.

question: Before selling or auctioning a repossessed vehicle, what opportunity must the lender's process give the borrower?

gold_references.title: Fair Practice Code 2023
gold_references.section_title: 9) Repossession of vehicles financed by Company
gold_references.evidence_snippet: a provision regarding final chance to be given to the borrower for repayment of loan before the sale / auction of the property
gold_references.reference_notes: The clause appears in the required repossession provisions of the loan agreement.

expected_information: The borrower must receive a final chance to repay before the secured property is sold or auctioned.

question: May a microfinance lender provide non-credit add-on products without the borrower's agreement, and where must their fees be stated?

gold_references.title: Fair Practices Code for Microfinance Loans
gold_references.section_title: 1. Applications for Loans and their processing
gold_references.evidence_snippet: Issuance of non-credit products shall be with the full consent of the borrowers and fee structure for such products shall be explicitly communicated to the borrower in the loan card itself
gold_references.reference_notes: The provision requires full borrower consent and disclosure of the fee structure in the loan card.

expected_information: Non-credit products require full borrower consent, and their fees must be clearly stated in the loan card.

question: If original property papers are lost or damaged after a personal loan is settled, what support and additional time does the code allow?

gold_references.title: Fair Practice Code (Version 7.1)
gold_references.section_title: 8. Responsible Lending Conduct — Release of movable/immovable property documents on repayment/settlement of personal loans
gold_references.evidence_snippet: In case of loss/damage to original movable/immovable property documents, either in part or in full, the Company shall assist the borrower in obtaining duplicate/certified copies of the movable/immovable property documents and shall bear the associated costs, in addition to paying compensation
gold_references.reference_notes: The same provision allows an additional 30 days for replacement-document steps; the delay penalty is calculated after a total period of 60 days.

expected_information: The lender must assist with obtaining duplicate/certified documents and bear the associated costs; an additional 30 days is allowed, with delay penalty calculated after a total of 60 days.
